top_news.title: GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra produces proof of the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture [pdf]
top_news.dek: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra model has provided a formal proof for the long-standing Cycle Double Cover Conjecture.
top_news.brief: The model successfully proved that every bridgeless undirected graph possesses a collection of cycles covering every edge exactly twice. This conjecture, originally posed by Tutte, Seymour, and others, has been a significant open problem in graph theory for decades.
top_news.image_alt: Mathematical graph theory diagram showing a cycle double cover

top_news.title: Ant Group’s Robbyant Unveils LingBot-VA 2.0: A Causal Video-Action Model Built Natively for Physical AI
top_news.dek: Ant Group's Robbyant releases LingBot-VA 2.0, a foundation model designed specifically for physical embodiment and high-frequency robotic control.
top_news.brief: LingBot-VA 2.0 is built from the ground up for physical AI rather than being fine-tuned from existing video generators. It utilizes a causal DiT architecture and sparse-MoE video streams to achieve 225 Hz asynchronous control. The model features Foresight Reasoning, allowing it to predict future states and re-ground observations in real-time for improved robotic execution.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing the LingBot-VA 2.0 causal video-action model architecture for robotic control.

top_news.title: AI Surveillance and Social Progress
top_news.dek: Bruce Schneier examines the societal implications of pervasive, AI-driven surveillance systems capable of real-time rule enforcement.
top_news.brief: Future AI surveillance systems may track public and private behavior, linking actions directly to government records. These systems function as automated, high-stakes enforcement tools that provide immediate alerts to authorities and the public for minor infractions, effectively scaling surveillance beyond traditional speed cameras.
top_news.image_alt: Conceptual illustration of AI-powered surveillance monitoring public spaces.

top_news.dek: OpenAI releases the GPT 5.6 series—Sol, Terra, and Luna—while transitioning Codex into a central superapp within the ChatGPT ecosystem.
top_news.brief: OpenAI has launched its latest frontier model series, GPT 5.6, comprising Sol, Terra, and Luna. Simultaneously, the company is pivoting Codex to serve as the core engine for a new ChatGPT superapp, signaling a shift toward more integrated, agentic workflows for developers and end-users.

primary.summary: In this post, you will learn four deployment patterns for taking models that have already been quantized with Unsloth and deploying them on AWS infrastructure. You also learn operational practices for production deployments.

primary.summary: We build an autonomous data science agent around DeepAnalyze-8B and run it end to end. We prepare a stable Colab runtime, install the machine-learning dependencies, and load the tokenizer and model in 4-bit mode to fit limited GPU memory. We add a sandboxed execution environment that lets the model generate Python, run it safely, observe results, and continue in an agentic loop.
